title: CoNP and SAT-oracle polynomial time
statement: Let a language be a set of finite binary strings. Define $	ext{NP}$ to consist of languages $L$ for which there are fixed nonnegative integers $C,c$ and a language $V$ decidable in deterministic polynomial time such that, for every string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ with $xu\in V$. Let $	ext{coNP}$ consist of languages whose complements belong to $	ext{NP}$. Let $	ext{SAT}$ be the language of binary strings whose decoded conjunctive normal form is satisfiable, with strings that fail to parse decoded as the empty formula. Let $	ext{P}^{\text{SAT}}$ consist of languages decidable by a deterministic oracle Turing machine with access to $	ext{SAT}$ in time at most $a(n^d+1)$ for some fixed nonnegative integers $a,d$. Then $\text{coNP}\subseteq\text{P}^{\text{SAT}}$.
